title: Mysuru Railway Museum and royal railway exhibits
content: Mysuru District Administration describes the Railway Museum as an outdoor collection opened in 1979 through railway official P. M. Joseph's efforts. Exhibits include vintage locomotives, material on the growth of Indian railways, and a royal train compartment used by Mysore's kings and queens, alongside objects associated with the former Srirangapatna railway station.
source_org: Mysuru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page does not provide a publication date or citations for the museum's historical account.
keywords: Mysuru railway museum royal train Mysore kings queens locomotives railway history Old Mysuru

title: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace in Bengaluru
content: The Bengaluru Urban district portal describes Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace as an Indo-Islamic building inside Bengaluru Fort. It says Hyder Ali began construction and Tipu Sultan completed it in 1791; after Tipu's death, the British administration used the palace as a secretariat until moving to Attara Kacheri in 1868. The Archaeological Survey of India maintains the site today.
source_org: Bengaluru Urban District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district portal provides no publication date or supporting historical references; dates are reproduced as stated by the portal.
keywords: Bengaluru Tipu Sultan summer palace Indo-Islamic architecture Bengaluru Fort Hyder Ali Mysore Kingdom Old Mysuru

title: Major crops and farmer services in Bengaluru Rural
content: The Bengaluru Rural Agriculture Department page identifies ragi as the district's principal crop, followed by fodder maize, redgram, cowpea, field bean and other crops. It describes the department's Raitha Samparka Kendras as channels for implementing agricultural programmes. The crop list is useful for distinguishing the district's dryland crop mix from the coastal and plantation profiles elsewhere in Karnataka.
source_org: Bengaluru Rural District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page gives no publication date or crop-area and production figures; it is not a current statistical series.
keywords: Bengaluru Rural ragi fodder maize redgram cowpea field bean crops agriculture farmer extension Old Mysuru

title: Ramanagara farm ponds and irrigation support in 2019-20
content: The current Bengaluru South district Agriculture Department page, indexed under SARVAM's existing Ramanagara district ID, reports that in 2019-20 the Krishi Bhagya programme constructed 685 farm ponds with subsidies totalling Rs 398.17 lakh. It also reports distribution of 3,118 sprinkler irrigation sets with Rs 479.84 lakh in subsidies, and farm machinery support to 1,771 farmers with Rs 640.4 lakh in subsidy. These are programme-reported counts and subsidy amounts for 2019-20, not present-day totals.
source_org: Bengaluru South District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal now uses Bengaluru South as the administrative name; SARVAM retains Ramanagara as its district ID. The page has no publication date, and these figures must not be presented as current.
keywords: Ramanagara Bengaluru South Krishi Bhagya farm ponds rainwater harvesting sprinkler irrigation farm machinery subsidy 2019-20 Old Mysuru

title: Sangama at the Shimsha-Kaveri confluence
content: Mandya District Administration identifies Sangama, also called Tore Kudala sthala, as the confluence of the Shimsha and Kaveri rivers. The portal lists it as a natural and scenic attraction in Mandya district, providing a district-specific example of the region's river landscape.
source_org: Mandya District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The tourism page is undated and gives no hydrological measurements.

title: Karighatta hill and Venkataramanaswamy temple
content: The Mandya district tourism page places Karighatta on the Lokapavani river's left bank near Srirangapatna and describes a hilltop Venkataramanaswamy temple associated with the Mysore kings. It reports the hill's elevation as 2,697 feet and describes the nearby meeting of the Kaveri and Lokapavani rivers. The page also notes historical spellings Karighatta and Karrighatta.
source_org: Mandya District Administration, Government of Karnataka
reporting_year: Not stated by source; fixed elevation from an undated tourism page
uncertainty: The elevation and historical statements are from an undated district tourism page without cited primary references.

title: Chamarajanagar's Southern Dry Zone landscape
content: The Chamarajanagar district portal places the district in Karnataka's Southern Dry Zone and describes undulating terrain with Eastern Ghats hill ranges, semi-arid rain-fed plains and forested hills in the Nilgiri region. It also notes that sericulture has been an important activity around Kollegal. This record captures the portal's district profile without treating its undated economic observations as current statistics.
source_org: Chamarajanagar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated. Its description of sericulture is qualitative and should not be read as a current measure of production or employment.
keywords: Chamarajanagar Southern Dry Zone rainfed semi-arid Eastern Ghats Nilgiri Kollegal sericulture geography Old Mysuru

title: Nandi Hills and Nandidurga history
content: The Chikkaballapura district portal describes Nandi Hills, formerly called Nandidurga, as a hill station at 1,478 metres above sea level. Its account says the site served as a summer retreat for Tipu Sultan and that Tipu and Hyder Ali expanded an earlier fort; the page also associates later gardens and bungalows with British rule. These are the district portal's historical claims, not independently dated archaeological findings.
source_org: Chikkaballapura District Administration, Government of Karnataka
reporting_year: Not stated by source; fixed altitude from an undated tourism page
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and does not cite sources for its historical narrative; altitude is reproduced as reported by the portal.

title: Shettihalli Church and the Hemavati reservoir
content: Hassan's district tourism page describes Shettihalli Church, also referred to as Sathalli in colonial documents, as a Gothic church built by French missionaries in the 1860s. The page says construction of the Hemavati Dam and reservoir in 1960 led to the church's abandonment and that it is partly submerged during monsoon seasons. The portal's page gives both a decade and a specific year for construction, so this record retains only the broader decade.
source_org: Hassan District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and is internally inconsistent about the church's exact construction year; the record uses its broader 1860s dating and attributes the account to the district portal.

title: Araluguppe Chennakeshava Temple
content: The Tumakuru district tourism portal describes the Chennakeshava Temple at Araluguppe as a Hoysala-period temple dedicated to Vishnu and attributes its construction in the 12th century to King Vishnuvardhana. The page describes a main shrine, mandapa, carved exterior and a stepped well within the temple complex. These architectural and historical details are recorded as the portal's account.
source_org: Tumakuru District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The tourism page is undated and provides no archaeological or inscription reference for the temple's dating and patronage.

title: Kolar's historic names and Chola-Ganga history
content: Kolar's district history page records older names including Kolahala, Kuvalala and Kolala, and describes the area as a historical frontier between northern Chalukya and southern Chola powers. The portal states that Cholas annexed Kolar in 1004 and held it until 1116, after which Western Ganga history remained important in the region. These dates and interpretations are attributed to the district portal rather than independently cross-checked here.
source_org: Kolar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and gives no citations for its chronology or place-name interpretations; dates are historical-event dates, not publication dates.
